title: code_review_phase_findings
description: Use this tool to submit your review as structured findings. Report every candidate issue you can anchor to an exact diff line, each with a calibrated confidence score: publishing decisions happen downstream at a configured confidence threshold, never in your head. An empty findings array is a valid and expected result for a clean diff.

findings.description: Every candidate issue you found, in the order you found them, including ones you consider minor or were unable to fully confirm — express doubt through the confidence score, never by omitting the finding. Anchor each one to an exact line of the diff: a finding you cannot anchor to a specific line, or that restates a design choice without identifying a concrete problem, does not belong here. Empty array when the diff is clean.

file.description: Full file path exactly as it appears in the diff.

new_line.description: Line number in the NEW version of the file, read from the `new_line` attribute of the `<line>` tag in the diff. Never guess, count, or interpolate: an approximate line number anchors the comment to the wrong code.

old_line.description: Line number in the OLD version, read from the `old_line` attribute of the `<line>` tag. Set this only for a deleted or unchanged context line.

target_code.description: Verbatim text content of the single `<line>` tag this finding is about, copied exactly character for character. This is what anchors the published comment, so it must match the file content exactly. A `suggestion`, when set, replaces exactly this line.

severity.description: critical: a correctness, safety, or security defect that should block merge. major: a likely-correctness, convention, or design problem that should be fixed. minor: optional or stylistic, informational only.

category.description: Short kebab-case slug for the issue TYPE, e.g. `sql-injection`, `layer-violation`, `missing-test`, `fail-open`. Rendered into the comment header and the summary breakdown, so prefer an established slug over inventing a near-synonym of one.

message.description: The finding in markdown: what the problem is and why it matters. Backtick code elements. Do NOT restate the severity or category — they render into the comment header automatically.

suggestion.description: Corrected version of the line in `target_code`, published as a suggestion the reader applies in one click. Code only, with that line's exact leading whitespace: no prose, explanatory comments, diff markers, or code fences. Set it whenever the fix is a rewrite of that one line. Leave it unset otherwise: moving, deleting, or splitting the line, changing the lines around it, and anchoring to a deleted line cannot be applied as a suggestion.

custom_instruction_ref.description: Name of the custom review instruction that drove this finding, when one did. Leave unset for findings from standard review criteria. Do not write the attribution into the message; it renders automatically from this field.

confidence.description: How sure you are the issue is REAL, scored on the evidence you gathered — not on how important it feels (that is severity). 9-10: you verified the defect and can point to the evidence. 6-8: likely real, but something material is unverified. 3-5: a plausible concern you could not settle either way; state the open question in the message. 0-2: a hunch supported by little. Never inflate the score to protect a finding from the publishing threshold.

summary.description: First-person recap of your review, 2-4 sentences: what you focused on, the kinds of issues you raised, and a rough estimate of the work needed to address them. When `findings` is empty, instead give 3-5 brief observation bullets (each starting with `- `) about the change: quality, tests, conventions. Do NOT include finding counts or per-severity tallies; those are computed and rendered separately.
